summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted from rehabilitation with fever, nausea, and coffee ground emesis. She had recently been hospitalized for pneumonia following CABG surgery. Evaluation revealed an upper gastrointestinal bleed likely due to a Mallory-Weiss tear, acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease possibly from medication effects or hemodynamic factors, and pulmonary edema from fluid overload, which was managed with diuresis. A urinary tract infection was treated with ciprofloxacin, and her nausea resolved with supportive care. A non-functioning PICC line was replaced with a central line for access. Her condition stabilized, kidney function improved, and she was discharged back to extended care with updated medications including omeprazole, increased diuretics, and adjusted blood pressure regimen, along with instructions to monitor weight and follow up for a repeat CT scan of the lung nodule in six months.
